extracted.intended_audience: Authors, reviewers, recommenders, and editors involved with mathematical & computational biology preprints
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and standards used by Peer Community In: Mathematical and Computational Biology to select, review, and recommend preprints in mathematical and computational biology, covering scope, quality, ethics, and procedural filters. Intended to direct authors on acceptable submissions and reviewers/recommenders on evaluation expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: High scientific, methodological, and ethical standards
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI Mathematical and Computational Biology recommends only preprints that meet high scientific, methodological, and ethical standards regardless of impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCI validates and publicly recommends peer-reviewed preprints by providing citable documentation that attests to methodological rigour and the validity of results and conclusions. Recommendation is based on methodological rigour and legitimacy of results rather than perceived impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data, code, and analysis sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires authors to share data, code, and analysis scripts with reviewers upon submission and with readers after recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sharing is compulsory at submission for reviewers' assessment and becomes public after recommendation; this supports reproducibility and verification of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Expects clear justification of sample sizes in empirical studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should provide rationale or calculations for chosen sample sizes to allow assessment of statistical power and appropriateness of inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness to replications, preregistered research, and negative results
rubrics_metrics.description: Welcomes replications, preregistered research, and negative results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCI explicitly values and encourages these types of studies as important contributions to robust science, reducing publication bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Does not accept submissions with financial conflicts of interest; other conflicts must be minimal and declared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCI also strives to ensure, as much as possible, that reviewers and recommenders are free from conflicts of interest related to the study or its authors. All relevant conflicts should be declared to preserve integrity of evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommender interest filter and 20-day rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Only preprints that attract the interest of at least one recommender are sent for peer review; submitted preprints that do not attract the interest of a recommender within a period of 20 days are not considered for evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommenders act similarly to associate editors and select work that stands out (to them) for its context, questions, methods, or findings. This is a procedural selection filter prior to formal peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical and methodological scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates preprints dealing with all fields of Mathematical and Computational Sciences applied to all fields of biology (examples listed: Neurobiology, Evolutionary Biology, Cell Biology, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCI is aimed at work at the interface of biology, mathematics, and computational science and welcomes articles exposing innovative models and/or methods with deep mathematical or computational content that contribute substantially to the advancement of the natural and biological sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discouraged topical/methodological content (out of scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not in scope: articles treating mathematical/computational problems only remotely inspired by biology and articles with elementary mathematical content or applying classic bio-informatic tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should have clear biological relevance and non-trivial mathematical/computational content; purely theoretical or elementary applications lacking substantial novelty or biological connection are unlikely to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed formats and discouraged submission types
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprints may have diverse formats: reviews, comments, opinion papers, research articles, data papers, technical notes, computer notes, movies, etc.; as a general rule, not interested in software papers that merely implement algorithms from existing literature without novel algorithmic techniques or insights, nor in papers that only/mainly benchmark existing software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCI encourages diverse formats but expects substantive novelty or insight beyond mere implementation or benchmarking; implementation/application to data is encouraged but not compulsory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation on implementation and application
rubrics_metrics.description: The implementation of methods and their application to data are encouraged but not compulsory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While empirical application and implemented methods strengthen manuscripts, theoretical or methodological advances without full implementation may still be considered if they substantially advance the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and exposition requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles are expected to be sufficiently well written to be understood superficially by any reader working at the interface of biology and mathematics or computational science; the objective of the work, the basic principles of the model/method, the relation to previous work, and the potential applications of the results should be accessible to a broad audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should explain objectives, principles, links to prior literature, and applications in accessible terms so non-specialists at the interface can grasp the contribution; clarity of exposition is a criterion for recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and conduct adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI Mathematical and Computational Biology subscribes to the principles of the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) and has its own code of conduct that users must comply with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All participants (authors, reviewers, recommenders, and board members) are expected to follow COPE principles and the PCI code of conduct; breaches may affect evaluation or participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusiveness and equity practices
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI is attentive to equity and inclusion at all stages of the scientific article evaluation process and focuses on bringing more people who are underrepresented in academia among authors, reviewers, recommenders, and board members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific recommendations and tools include: possibility to submit articles anonymously, transparency in evaluation, Managing Board members considering underrepresentation when appointing recommenders, template messages to encourage equity, possibility to review anonymously, and alignment with Coalition for Diversity and Inclusion in Scholarly Communication (C4DISC) principles.
